Exteriors

Siding Repair

Damaged siding is a water problem before it is an appearance problem.

Schedule a Free Inspection 469-371-9599
  • Free inspectionsLicensed inspector, on your roof
  • Free estimatesWritten, itemised, no obligation
  • Fully insuredCover in place before we start
  • Licensed inspectorsAssessing, not selling
  • DFW and North TexasRoughly two hours from Dallas

Most North Texas homes are predominantly brick, with siding on gables, dormers, and rear elevations. Those are exactly the areas that take wind-driven rain and hail, and they are frequently the last part of the exterior anyone looks at.

Repairs matter because siding is a water management layer. Cracked panels and open trim joints let moisture behind the cladding, where it does quiet damage to sheathing and framing.

When siding repair is worth looking into

Cracked, split, or punctured panels

Frequently hail impact on gable ends.

Loose or rattling sections

Wind has broken the fastening or the lock.

Soft trim at corners and windows

Water is getting in at the joints.

Staining or peeling below joints

Evidence of water tracking behind the surface.

Free exterior inspection

A licensed inspector, photographs you keep, and a written estimate — at no cost and no obligation.

Causes

What causes it

Hail impact

Gable ends facing the storm take direct hits.

Wind-driven rain

Water pushed sideways into joints that shed vertical rain fine.

Sun exposure

UV embrittles some materials and finishes on west-facing walls.

Failed caulking at transitions

Where siding meets brick, trim, or roof lines.

Our inspection

How we look at it

  • Identify the siding material before recommending anything
  • Check gable ends and elevations exposed to storm direction
  • Inspect trim, transitions, and penetrations
  • Look for evidence of moisture behind the cladding
  • Assess how well replacement material will match

North Texas conditions

On the brick-and-siding combination typical of North Texas suburbs, the siding sections are usually high gables that nobody inspects from the ground — and those are the surfaces that take the worst of a wind-driven hail storm.

Process

How the work runs

01

Inspection

Material identified, damage extent documented.

02

Estimate

Free, with a frank assessment of match quality.

03

Repair

Damaged sections replaced and transitions properly sealed.

04

Finish

Painting where the material requires it, and cleanup.

05

Moisture check behind the cladding

We look at what the water has been doing to the sheathing, not only at the cracked panel.

06

Finish and cleanup

Painting where the material needs it, and the site left clean.

Options

Materials and approaches

Section replacement

Replacing damaged panels or boards.

Trim and transition repair

Rebuilding the joints where water actually enters.

Full elevation replacement

Where damage is widespread or matching is impossible.

Trim and corner replacement

The joints where water actually gets in, rebuilt rather than resealed.

Sheathing repair

Replacing board that has already taken on moisture behind the cladding.

Caulk and seal refresh

Renewing the joints at windows, corners, and transitions where the cladding itself is still sound.

Not sure which of these you need?

That is what the free inspection is for. A licensed inspector will tell you what your roof actually requires.

Questions

Siding Repair FAQs

Will repaired siding match?

Rarely perfectly on a weathered wall. We will tell you honestly what to expect before starting rather than after.

Should siding be inspected after hail?

Yes. Gable siding damage is common and frequently missed because everyone is looking at the roof.
